text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said state governments which have exempted property developers from building low-cost houses within their project sites will be asked to explain their decision. Developers have to allocate 30 percent of their housing projects for low-cost houses under a government ruling.

-- In a landmark decision, the High Court has ordered highway operator Projek Lebuhraya Utara-Selatan (PLUS) to pay 120,000 ringgit ($48,000) to the widow of a motorist who was killed when his vehicle hit a stray cow along the north-south expressway.

-- Acting PM Anwar said cities in developing nations must not be cold and violence-stricken but instead nurtured into sanctuaries for the people to earn a decent living and raise families. He was speaking at the opening of the South-South Mayors Conference in Kuala Lumpur.
-- Some 100 local and foreign firms have applied to be listed on Malaysia's planned over-the-counter market for high-growth companies Mesdaq, said Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar.
